limitations: No first-hand benchmark was run; all performance numbers are supplier-reported.
No onboarding duration is published by any source, so the article counts steps and admin dependencies and does not quote hours.
The pricing capture contains unrelated consumer copy; only the plan/feature table structure was used.
CodeQL language/build-mode coverage is deliberately not summarised; readers are sent to GitHub's own matrix.
SARIF/alert-export and compliance-artefact questions are stated as documentation gaps on two pages, not as vendor capability verdicts.
Bitbucket support for Bugbot is carried with its public-beta qualifier.
Demand evidence is the selection's frozen 2026-10-19 baseline and was not re-measured.

Correction pass 2 changed only the coverage-matrix licence row, the YAML key inventory, the rule-model paragraphs and the revision note; every figure, the billing arithmetic, the CodeQL section and the no-download evidence statement are unchanged from the version the reviewer already checked.

The License Scan is documented as an invoked step inside a rule example, so the article describes it as rule-triggered and does not claim it runs by default; whether an unconfigured repository gets any licence coverage is not stated on the page and is not asserted here.

Rule-text inclusion order and YAML settings precedence are two different documented lists; the article keeps them separate and does not infer precedence between contradictory rule sources, which the page leaves undocumented.
